## 2026-10-11 — PR: claude/pile-o36 (PR link added after merge)

### F26, part c. Depth to fixity z_fix: wording says what the depth is (first moment reversal below M_max, and which zero of the moment diagram that is for the head condition); every depth-to-fixity line labelled on the elevation; H-pile section label moved off the lines   [UI only] [no calculation change]
- **Date:** 2026-10-11. **Type:** display / wording only. Engineer's comment 2026-10-11 (via the coordinator): the label "z_fix 15.8 ft (2nd M zero)" is confusing, because on a free-head pile the line sits at the FIRST zero crossing below grade (the head's M = 0 is the "1st zero"); in the H-pile elevation the 5 % decay dashed line (≈ 14.6 ft) had no label and the "HP 13.83×14.70 (strong axis)…" label sat on it.
- **The rule (unchanged, `momentZeroCrossings(z, M).second`, anchor `second: below.length ? below[0].z : null,   // first reversal BELOW Mmax`):** z_fix is the FIRST zero crossing of the moment below the depth of the largest below-grade |M|, searched over the embedded length only (the stickup is excluded), ignoring crossings whose preceding lobe is < 2 % of that moment, linearly interpolated between nodes. Which zero of the whole moment diagram that is depends on the head:
  - free head, no applied head moment, no rotational restraint (M = 0 at the head): the head counts as the 1st zero, so z_fix is normally the **2nd zero** of the moment diagram (k + 1, k = its rank among the below-grade crossings);
  - head moment ≠ 0 (fixed head, rotational restraint `pyKrot` > 0, or an applied head moment `pyMhead`): the head is not a zero; z_fix is the **k-th zero crossing below grade**: the **1st** when the largest below-grade moment is the lobe at grade (H-pile defaults, fixed head: z_fix 2.4 ft, crossings 2.42 / 17.57 / 30.0 ft), the **2nd** when the next lobe down is larger (micropile defaults, fixed head: z_fix 10.7 ft, crossings 1.23 / 10.74 / 15.45 ft); micropile defaults, free head with M_head 5 kip·ft: 1st below grade (10.9 ft).
  - So the old wording "2nd zero-crossing of the moment diagram" was right only for the free head without head moment; the depth itself is unchanged in every case.
- **New helper** after `momentZeroCrossings` (anchor `function pyZfixWords(pyRes, I) {`): returns `{ short, long, nth }` for a p-y result, `nth` = the head-specific sentence above (from the rank of `pyRes.zFix2` in `pyRes.mzCrossings`, `I.solverHead`, `I.pyKrot`, `I.pyMhead`); null when there is no z_fix.
- **Text changes (before → after; value unchanged):**
  | where (anchor) | before | after |
  |---|---|---|
  | `latKV` key values: line name (legend on the Lateral graphs, elevation label, report figure) (`const zw = pyZfixWords(pyRes, I);`) | `z_fix 15.8 ft (2nd M zero)` | `z_fix 15.8 ft (1st M reversal below Mmax)` (M_max in the stickup: `… below peak below-grade M`) |
  | `latKV` line definition (hover, key-values strip on screen and in the report) | `z_fix = 15.8 ft — 2nd zero crossing of moment (Module 02, reference)` | `z_fix = 15.8 ft — first moment reversal (zero crossing) below M_max; here the 2nd zero of the moment diagram, counting M = 0 at the free head as the 1st (Module 02, reference)` (fixed head: `… below the largest below-grade moment (M_max is in the stickup; the search runs over the embedded length); here the 1st zero crossing below grade (fixed head: the head moment is not zero, so the head does not count) …`) |
  | elevation caption (`purple solid = z_fix (`) | `(2nd moment zero, Module 02 reference)` | `(first moment reversal below M_max, Module 02 reference)` |
  | Module 02 "Geotechnical depth to fixity" (`first moment reversal (zero crossing) below M", /*#__PURE__*/`) | `z_fix = 10.7 ft below mudline · 2nd zero-crossing of the moment diagram (first reversal below Mmax @ 4.1 ft)` | `z_fix = 10.7 ft below mudline · first moment reversal (zero crossing) below Mmax @ 4.1 ft · here the 2nd zero of the moment diagram, counting M = 0 at the free head as the 1st` |
  | Module 02, no z_fix | `…, so there is no second zero-crossing. (Short …)` | `…, so there is no z_fix. (Short …)` |
  | report 02R "Geotechnical depth to fixity" (`" below mudline · first moment reversal (zero crossing) below " + (pyRes.MmaxAboveGrade`) | `z_fix = 10.7 ft below mudline · 2nd zero-crossing of the moment diagram` | `z_fix = 10.7 ft below mudline · first moment reversal (zero crossing) below Mₘₐₓ @ 4.1 ft · here the 2nd zero …` |
  | report, no z_fix | `…; there is no second zero-crossing.` | `…; there is no z_fix.` |
  | Methodology "Two paths…" (linear solver) | `depth to fixity as the second zero-crossing of the moment diagram` | `depth to fixity as the first zero crossing of the moment below the maximum moment (on a free-head pile with no head moment, the 2nd zero of the moment diagram, counting M = 0 at the head)` |
  | report narrative, linear source | `(second zero-crossing of the moment diagram)` | `(the first zero crossing of the moment below the maximum moment)` |
  | buckling "stiffness match" note | `which is the second zero-crossing of the moment diagram.` | `which is the first moment reversal (zero crossing) below the maximum moment.` |
  | linear-Winkler panel: hover, derivation line, note | `fixity (2nd moment zero)`, `L_f = … ft (2nd moment zero)`, `Fixity = 2nd zero-crossing of the moment diagram.` | `fixity (1st moment zero below Mmax)`, `L_f = … ft (1st moment zero below M_max)`, `Fixity = first zero crossing of the moment below the maximum moment.` (that legacy value keeps its fallback chain, first crossing then 0.3·e, when there is no reversal below M_max; unchanged) |
- **Elevation (`ElevationPlot`):**
  - every depth-to-fixity line is now labelled on a wide card (before: only the first, normally z_fix): the shallowest line's label above it at the right, the deepest's below it at the right (shifted 100 px left of the edge, clear of the soil-layer name), a middle one above it at the left of the moment panel (anchor `const zs = kv.fix.map(g => g.z).sort((a, b) => a - b), nF = zs.length;`). Narrow card: unchanged (no line labels; all in the hover and the key strip).
  - H-pile section label ("HP 13.83×14.70 (strong axis): width d = 13.83 in"): at mid-depth as before unless a depth-to-fixity line is within 16 px; then at the depth between 20 % and 80 % of grade-to-toe farthest from every line (anchor `const yMidHP = (() => {`). H-pile defaults: from 15.0 ft (on the 14.6 ft decay line) to ≈ 6.0 ft.
- **Governing provision:** none (display wording). No formula, factor, unit, code reference, saved key or format changes.

+/* F26 c (display only): wording for the depth to fixity z_fix (pyRes.zFix2). The rule is

+   the largest below-grade |M| (embedded length only; lobes < 2 % of that moment ignored).

+     - free head with no head moment (M = 0 at the head, no rotational restraint): the head
+       counts as the 1st zero, so z_fix is the (k+1)-th zero, k = its rank among the
+       below-grade crossings (normally the 2nd zero);
+     - head moment != 0 (fixed head, rotational restraint or an applied head moment): the
+       head is not a zero; z_fix is the k-th zero crossing below grade (1st when the

### F27. p-y first attempts: the stable-branch test applies to them too (O36); force-closure residual normalised for a moment-only head load   [calc behaviour / check status] [MORE conservative: a first attempt that converged on a post-critical state (head deflection reversed or folding back) is no longer used; it goes to the retry and, in every case found, ends "did not converge" with the lateral-dependent checks NG. The closure change alters only the displayed ΣF % of moment-only head loads and the acceptance of retried solves with no lateral load (none found)]
- **Date:** 2026-10-11. **Type:** calc behaviour (acceptance of a numerical solution) + diagnostic normalisation.
- **Engineer's decision 2026-10-11 on O36:** "yes apply it to first attempts too." Coordinator's ruling after the first implementation was stopped (below): first attempts get (a) and (c) only ("the same stable-branch test"); (b) closure stays for retried solves; fix the ΣF normalisation for P_t = 0; the layered-profile residual is logged as O38 and not changed.
- **Where:**
  - `pyRetryCheck` (anchor `function pyRetryCheck(rr, D, branchOnly) {`): new third argument `branchOnly`; when true the closure test is skipped.
  - `solvePyWithRetry` (anchor `const why1 = res.ok ? pyRetryCheck(res, D, true) : null;`): the converged first attempt is checked; if rejected, the retry runs; new result field `firstWhy`; "did not converge" reasons now say whether the first attempt did not converge or converged but was rejected (and why).
  - `solvePyPile`, closure (anchor `fPct: 100 * Math.abs(fRes) / Math.max(Math.abs(Pt), 0.01 * intAbsP, 1e-6),`).
  - `App` → `pyRes` (anchor `retried: sol.retried, firstWhy: sol.firstWhy,`); `PyPanel` Module 02 banner (anchor `pyRes.firstWhy && pyRes.firstWhy.length`); the block comment above `PY_NC_MSG`, the comment above `PY_DEFL_WARN_D_DEFAULT`; Methodology paragraph "Nonlinear p-y convergence".
  - Everything that calls `solvePyWithRetry` takes the new rule: Module 02 (`pyRes`) and "Run all cases" (`runAllCases`), so the envelope still equals Module 02 for the active case. Not affected: the Module 10 nonlinear P-crit ramp (`computePcr` → `runOneCasePcr` calls `solvePyPile` directly; non-convergence and a deflection sign flip are its designed end points, LPile Tech Manual 4.4.2; it does not use this acceptance) and the integral-abutment Tier-2 solve (`iabNonlinearSolve` calls `solvePyPile` directly). Their results are unchanged (the `eq` field they get is not used by them).
- **Governing provision:** none. The acceptance tests and the closure measure are numerical-solution criteria chosen by the tool (judgement values, as F22/F25), not code provisions. No AASHTO formula, load or resistance factor, unit or code reference changes.
- **Acceptance rule, before → after:**
  | test | first attempt, before (F22/F25) | first attempt, after (F27) | retried solve (unchanged) |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | (a) every load step converged | required | required | required |
  | (b) closure ΣF ≤ 1 % and ΣM ≤ 1 % | not tested | **not tested** (see "Why not (b)" below) | required |
  | (c) stable branch: head deflection keeps the sign of step 1 and never drops > 0.1 % below its running peak | not tested | **required** | required |
  - Flow: first attempt converges and passes (c) → used (bit-identical to before); converges but fails (c) → retry; retry passes (a)–(c) → used, Module 02 adds "(The first solve (8 load steps) converged but was rejected: <reason>.)"; otherwise "Did not converge" (F22 NG behaviour) with the reason, e.g. "the first solve (8 load steps) converged but was rejected: the head deflection reversed direction during the load ramp (post-critical equilibrium); the adaptive retry (16 load steps) was rejected: …". The F25 large-deflection warning is unchanged.
- **Before / after (`pyRetryCheck`, `solvePyWithRetry`):**
  ```js
  // before
  function pyRetryCheck(rr, D) {
    const why = [];
    const eq = rr.eq || {};
    if (!(eq.fPct <= PY_RETRY_CLOSURE_PCT && eq.mPct <= PY_RETRY_CLOSURE_PCT))
  …
  function solvePyWithRetry(input, D) {
    const res = solvePyPile({ ...input, nSteps: 8, maxIter: 200 });
    if (res.ok) return { res, retried: false, noConv: false, why: [] };
    const res2 = …
  // after
  function pyRetryCheck(rr, D, branchOnly) {
    const why = [];
    const eq = rr.eq || {};
    if (!branchOnly && !(eq.fPct <= PY_RETRY_CLOSURE_PCT && eq.mPct <= PY_RETRY_CLOSURE_PCT))
  …
  function solvePyWithRetry(input, D) {
    const res = solvePyPile({ ...input, nSteps: 8, maxIter: 200 });
    const why1 = res.ok ? pyRetryCheck(res, D, true) : null;
    if (res.ok && !why1.length) return { res, retried: false, noConv: false, why: [], firstWhy: null };
    const first = res.ok
      ? "the first solve (8 load steps) converged but was rejected: " + why1.join("; ")
      : "the first solve (8 load steps) did not converge";
    const res2 = …   (retry unchanged; messages prefixed with `first`)
    return { res: res2, retried: true, noConv: false, why: [], firstWhy: res.ok ? why1 : null };
  ```
  (full diff at the end of this entry).
- **Closure normalisation, before → after (`solvePyPile`, `res.eq.fPct`; ΣM unchanged):**
  - Before: `fPct = 100·|ΣF residual| / max(|P_t|, 1e-6 lb)`. With no lateral load (a moment-only head load) the divisor is 1e-6 lb, so any round-off residual shows as 10 % to 2e6 % (uniform soil) or 1e10 % (layered).
  - After: `fPct = 100·|ΣF residual| / max(|P_t|, 0.01·∫|p| dz, 1e-6 lb)`, ∫|p| dz = the total soil-reaction magnitude along the pile (trapezoidal, same nodes as the residual). Chosen so that nothing changes when there is a lateral load: in every solve run with P_t ≠ 0 (338 converged first attempts and retries with P_t ≠ 0, uniform and four-layer, both pile types, free and fixed head), |P_t| ≥ 1/38 of ∫|p| dz, so |P_t| governs. Only when P_t is (near) zero does the soil reaction set the scale. ΣM already divides by max(∫|p|·z dz, |M_head|), which does not vanish under a moment-only load, so it is unchanged.
  - Effect: displayed "equilibrium closure ΣF" in Module 02, the report 02R table and the solver note, and the retry acceptance test (b). A first attempt is never rejected by it (F27 does not test (b) on first attempts).
  - **Worked check (moment-only), micropile defaults, free head, STL 86 / P 0 / M_head 5 kip·ft:** ΣF residual = 0.01136 lb (from 1.136e6 % × 1e-6 lb); ∫|p| dz = 2,838 lb; divisor before 1e-6 lb → 1,136,024 %; after max(0, 28.38 lb, 1e-6) = 28.38 lb → 0.01136 / 28.38 = **0.040 %**. ΣM 0.000235 % (unchanged). Mmax 6.02 kip·ft, y₀ 0.197 in, flexure 0.112 OK, combined 0.281 OK: unchanged, and the solve is used (before and after).
  - Other moment-only cases (displayed ΣF before → after; nothing else changes): micropile M 40: 1.89e6 % → 0.0071 %; H-pile defaults M 5: 10.55 % → 8.3e-7 %; H-pile M 40: 4.0e5 % → 0.0039 %. Four-layer profile (layered residual, O38): micropile M 5 at STL 20/86/150: 8.8e9/6.9e9/1.07e10 % → 253/173/227 %; H-pile M 5: 8.5e9–9.9e9 % → 115–132 %; M 40: 2.1e11 % → 1,049–1,057 %. These layered values are still large; they are the O38 residual, not a moment-only artefact.
- **Why not (b) on first attempts (the first implementation was stopped):** with (b) also applied to first attempts, ordinary converged solves became "did not converge": every moment-only head load (closure 1e6 %), and every four-layer profile case, because a first attempt on a layered profile shows a large force residual on main already (four-layer H-pile defaults ΣF 43.80 % / ΣM 15.06 %, micropile 3.17 % / 1.10 %; see O38). The coordinator ruled (a) + (c) for first attempts.
- **Worked case (i) — micropile defaults, free head, one strength case STL 20 kip / P 15 kip** (O36 example; D = 7.00 in):
  - First attempt (8 steps of 1.875 kip / 2.5 kip): converges; head deflection by step +0.398, +0.998, +1.774, +2.761, +3.978, +5.461, +7.331, **−164.69 in** (step 8, sign reversal). Closure ΣF 0.0059 %, ΣM 0.00089 %.
  - Before: used. Module 02 Mmax **130.41 kip·ft** @ 3.8 ft, y₀ −164.69 in; flexure D/C 2.417 NG, combined 2.457 NG, casing extension OK, combined-loading stability **OK**; `allPass` false; envelope row 130.41 / −164.694 / 2.42 / 2.46.
  - After: (c) fails (reversal at step 8) → retry (16 steps): +0.162 … +7.331 (step 14), +9.221 (step 15), step 16 does not converge within 400 iterations → **"Did not converge"**, reason "the first solve (8 load steps) converged but was rejected: the head deflection reversed direction during the load ramp (post-critical equilibrium); the adaptive retry (16 load steps, under-relaxed) did not converge; the retry stopped at load step 16/16 (lateral 15.00 kip, axial 20.0 kip)". Flexure, combined, casing extension, uncased flexure and stability NG; `allPass` false; envelope row n/c, NG (equals Module 02). Lateral graphs tab: "No graphs are shown: the lateral p-y analysis did not converge" with the reason (screenshot looked at).
  - Hand check of (c): y₁ = +0.398 in > 0; y₈ = −164.69 in; y₈·y₁ < 0 → reversal → reject.
- **Worked case (ii) — micropile defaults (default soil), cases Ext I 60 kip / 12 kip / M 5 kip·ft (active) and Str I 86 / 6:**
  - Before: Ext I first attempt used: y₀ **−47.04 in**, Mmax 112.77 kip·ft, closure 0.0013 % / 0.00016 %, flexure 2.090 NG, combined 2.209 NG, stability OK; envelope Ext I 112.77 / −47.037 / 2.09 / 2.18.
  - After: (c) fails (reversal) → retry converges but also reverses → rejected by (c) → **"Did not converge"**, NG; envelope Ext I n/c. Str I row unchanged (53.70 kip·ft, y₀ 3.201 in, flexure 0.995, combined 1.165).
- **Worked case (iii) — no change where the first attempt is on the stable branch (bit-identical):** parity (`parity.mjs`, the F26 c commit vs this commit; micropile, H-pile, integral abutment, edited micropile: page text, printed report, module statuses, check strip, autosave, Save .json export, IndexedDB record, share payload):
  - defaults: identical in every mode;
  - four-layer profile: identical in every mode (micropile closure 3.17 % / 1.10 %, H-pile 43.80 % / 15.06 %: shown as before; these first attempts are on the stable branch);
  - four-layer + buckling: identical for H-pile; **changed** for the two micropile cases whose first attempt is post-critical (listed below). The integral-abutment report changes only because it prints the micropile p-y figure, which is no longer drawn for the post-critical state.
- **Worked case (iv) — H-pile defaults, free head, STL 800 / P 120:** first attempt does not converge (step 7), so F27 does not apply; unchanged: "Did not converge", reason "the first solve (8 load steps) did not converge; the adaptive retry (16 load steps) was rejected: the head deflection reversed direction during the load ramp (post-critical equilibrium)"; Module 04/05/stability NG; envelope n/c.
- **Every case found that changes result** (all MORE conservative; all had a reversed head deflection on main, and the retry also reversed or did not converge — no retried solve was accepted anywhere):
  | case | main | after |
  |---|---|---|
  | (i) micropile defaults, STL 20 / P 15 | y₀ −164.69 in, Mmax 130.41, stability OK | did not converge, NG |
  | (ii) micropile defaults, Ext I 60 / 12 / M 5 active | y₀ −47.04 in, Mmax 112.77, stability OK | did not converge, NG |
  | four-layer + buckling (L_u 8 ft), micropile defaults | y₀ −19.55 in, Mmax 78.1, closure 5.12 % / 0.83 %; Module 02 status "—" | did not converge (reversal; retry stopped at step 13/16), Module 02 NG; checks not satisfied 5 → 6 |
  | four-layer + buckling, edited micropile (bond 31 ft) | y₀ −16.08 in, Mmax 50.1, **casing flexure (04) OK** | did not converge (reversal; retry closure 5.51 % and reversal), 02 and 04 NG; checks not satisfied 3 → 5 |
  | sweep, uniform default soil (below) | 38 micropile first attempts with y₀ −4.7 to −178 in used | all 38 → did not converge |
  | sweep, four-layer profile (below) | 8 micropile first attempts with y₀ −10.9 to −35.4 in used | all 8 → did not converge |
- **Sweep (diagnostic copy of the branch recording every `solvePyWithRetry` call through "Run all cases", M-φ curves at the sweep's axial):**
  - Uniform default soil, free head, P 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20 kip × STL 20, 40, 60, 86, 100, 120, 150, 200 kip, micropile and H-pile (208 solves): 193 first attempts converged; 155 pass (c) → used as before (closure of these ≤ 0.0011 % ΣF / 0.00022 % ΣM); 38 (micropile only; STL 20–86 from P 10–16 up, STL 100–150 from P 5–8 up, STL 200 from P 3) reverse → retry → rejected by (c) (33) or not converged (5) → did not converge. All 104 H-pile solves unchanged. 15 first attempts did not converge (unchanged path).
  - Mixed set, micropile and H-pile, free and fixed head (P 0–20, STL 0–200, head moments 0, ±5…±40, service / tension / extreme rows, negative P; 52 solves): 48 unchanged; 4 micropile reversed first attempts (fixed head STL 200 / P 20; free head 60 / 12 / M 5, 150 / 10, 200 / 20) → did not converge. Opposing head moment (P 6 / M −10, P 4 / M −20) and negative P: stable branch, unchanged.
  - Four-layer profile, free head, STL 20, 86, 150 × P 1–20 and moment-only / P 1 + M 20 (66 solves): 55 first attempts unchanged (including all H-pile; closures with a lateral load up to 52 % ΣF / 15 % ΣM, see O38), 8 micropile reversed → did not converge, 3 not converged first (unchanged path).
  - Closure: with (b) not applied to first attempts, no first attempt is rejected for closure. Across the uniform-soil sweep the first-attempt closure never exceeded 0.052 % ΣF / 0.010 % ΣM (including the reversed ones); the large values seen are all the layered-profile residual (O38) or (before F27) the moment-only divisor.
- **Saved data:** none changed (`firstWhy` is run-time only).
- **How verified:** node --check of every script block; headless Chromium with the pinned libraries served locally: `o37.mjs` per worked case (main vs branch: `pyRes`, `R`, Module 02 text, envelope, dashboard, report), `parity.mjs` (above), `sweep.mjs` with a diagnostic copy for the sweep, a test copy forcing a first-attempt rejection to exercise the "converged but was rejected … converged on the adaptive retry" display (micropile defaults: retry accepted, Mmax 53.45 kip·ft, same as the first attempt to 4 digits, text shown). Screenshots looked at: Module 02 "did not converge" banner for case (i), Lateral graphs tab did-not-converge state, envelope, dashboard. No console errors.
- **Other copies of this code:** none.

## 2026-10-11 — PR: claude/pile-o38 (PR link added after merge)

### F28. Equilibrium closure from the soil reaction the solver applied (O38); Soil reaction graph and Figure F-3 points show that reaction   [diagnostic + display] [no result change: y, M, V, M_max, y₀ and every D/C are bit-identical; the displayed closure changes, and so does the closure the retry acceptance test (b) reads — no accept / reject outcome changed in 326 solves]
- **Date:** 2026-10-11. **Type:** diagnostic (closure measure) + display (graphs). No formula, load or resistance factor, unit or code reference changes.
- **Engineer's decision 2026-10-11 on O38:** "yes do both, switch the soil reaction graph too" — (1) the closure integrates the reaction the solver applied; (2) apply the closure test (b) to first attempts too; (3) plot the solver-applied reaction on the Soil reaction graph. **Item (2) is NOT in this entry:** the required re-run found ordinary converged solves that (b) would reject (four-layer H-pile, moment-only head load M 40 kip·ft, see "Item (2) withheld" below and O39). Per the instruction ("if any ordinary solve is rejected by (b), STOP and report") it was stopped and is left for a decision. First attempts keep (a) + (c) only, as F27.
- **Cause of O38 (found by the investigation, confirmed here):** the soft-clay (Matlock) and stiff-clay (Welch & Reese) p-y models have a secant floor `yFloor = 0.001·y₅₀` (× f_y) in `pySecantEs`: below |y| = 0.001·y₅₀ the solver uses the secant stiffness through the floor point, i.e. it linearises the curve (needed because the y^(1/3) / y^(1/4) curves have infinite initial slope). The FD stiffness rows use that E_s. The closure, however, integrated `res.p = pyPofY(y)`, the curve itself, which at those near-zero-deflection nodes is far above E_s·y (p ∝ y^(1/4) vs p ∝ y; up to ~50× at 23 ft in the example). On a four-layer profile with 9 ft of stiff clay under the active zone, 32 of 121 nodes are below the floor and the curve values add 2.6 kip of "reaction" that the solver never applied. The solution itself is sound: recomputed with the applied reaction the closure is 0.006 % / 0.004 %.
- **Where:**
  - `solvePyPile` (anchor `res.pEq.push(pySecantEs(soil[i].model, y[IX(i)], z[i], soil[i].prm, gPM, gYM) * y[IX(i)]);`): new result array `res.pEq` = E_s(y)·y at each node, with the same `pySecantEs` call (same yFloor, f_m, f_y) the FD rows use; `res.p` is unchanged and kept. The closure loop (`intP`, `intPz`, `intAbsPz`) and the F27 force-normalisation integral `intAbsP` now integrate `res.pEq` (anchor `const pE = res.pEq;`).
  - `App` → `pyRes`: `pNode: res2.pEq` (was `res2.p`; anchor `pNode: res2.pEq,`) and `mobil` (anchor `Math.abs(res2.pEq[i2]) / pu2`).
  - `PyCurvesFig` note (anchor `p = the reaction the solver applied (E_s·y, the secant stiffness times y)`), with a sentence naming any depth whose ● lies off its curve; `LatGraphsCard` → `soil` panel notes (anchors `Solver-applied reaction: the nodal soil reaction p = E_s·y` and `p = the solver-applied reaction beside it`); Methodology paragraph "Nonlinear p-y convergence" (closure basis E_s·y stated); graphics header comment.
- **Governing provision:** none (a numerical-solution diagnostic and a display choice). The p-y models, the yFloor linearisation, the solve and all results are unchanged.
- **Before / after (`solvePyPile`):**
  ```js
  // before
      res.p.push(pyPofY(soil[i].model, y[IX(i)], z[i], soil[i].prm, gPM, gYM));
    }

      intPz += 0.5 * (res.p[i] * z[i] + res.p[i + 1] * z[i + 1]) * h;

  // after

The closure formulas themselves (ΣF = P_t − ∫p dz over max(|P_t|, 0.01∫|p|dz); ΣM = M_head + Q_t(y₀ − y_toe) + ∫p·z dz over max(∫|p|·z dz, |M_head|)) are unchanged; only p changes from the curve value to the applied value.
- **Hand check of one node (four-layer H-pile defaults, z = 23.13 ft, Welch & Reese stiff clay, b = 14.70 in, ε₅₀ = 0.006, f_m·p_u = 2,296.9 lb/in, y = 1.1896e-6 in; Figure F-3 with that depth):**
  - y₅₀ = 2.5·ε₅₀·b = 2.5 × 0.006 × 14.70 = 0.2205 in; floor = 0.001 × 0.2205 = 2.205e-4 in > |y| → linearised.
  - Curve (before, `res.p`): p = 0.5·p_u·(y/y₅₀)^0.25 = 1,148.45 × (5.395e-6)^0.25 = 1,148.45 × 0.04819 = **55.35 lb/in**.
  - Applied (after, `res.pEq`): E_s = 0.5·p_u·(0.001)^0.25 / floor = 1,148.45 × 0.17783 / 2.205e-4 = 926,200 lb/in²; p = E_s·y = 926,200 × 1.1896e-6 = **1.10 lb/in**. (Above the floor the two are equal: the 3.88 ft sand and 12.13 ft clay rows show |p − p(y)| = 0.)

Cause: with P_t = 0 the force residual is normalised by 0.01·∫|p|dz (F27); the absolute residual is 1.68 lb against ∫|p|dz = 12,797 lb, i.e. the solver's convergence tolerance (tol 1e-6): with tol 1e-9 the same solve gives 0.0016 % (M_max 40.54425 → 40.54426 kip·ft). Max closure of the first attempts that would be accepted: uniform 0.0011 % / 0.00022 %; mixed set 0.040 % / 0.00056 %; four-layer 0.096 % / 0.021 % (lateral load). Logged as O39.

- **Saved data:** none changed (`pEq` is run-time only; no storage key or export format touched).
- **How verified:** node --check of every script block; headless Chromium with the pinned libraries served locally: `parity.mjs` main vs branch (micropile, H-pile, integral abutment, edited micropile × default soil, four-layer, four-layer + buckling: page text, printed report, module statuses, check strip, autosave, Save .json export, IndexedDB record, share payload) — identical except the closure numbers listed above and the retry reason of the four-layer + buckling edited micropile; `latg.mjs` (Lateral graphs: soil-reaction trace, F-3 table and notes, with automatic and user depths); `sweeps.sh` / `swcmp.py` (above); `m40.mjs` (tolerance check of the moment-only case). ### F26, part d. Davisson & Robinson depth to fixity on the lateral graphs, always, as the primary labelled fixity line, with an AASHTO reference   [UI only] [no calculation change]
- **Date:** 2026-10-11. **Type:** display only. No new calculation: the value is Module 10's `Lf_davisson`.
- **Engineer's request 2026-10-11:** "yes add it, make sure it [is] labeled with a AASHTO reference as well." Show the Davisson & Robinson (1965) depth to fixity on the lateral graphs always (not only with buckling enabled), as the primary labelled line on F-1, the elevation and the soil-reaction plot; z_fix and the 5 % decay depth as secondary lines; the Module 10 buckling line only when buckling is on and its method is not Davisson; also in the printed figures and key strips.
- **Value and datum:** `r.buckling.Lf_davisson = davissonMult × davissonChar` (1.8·T, T = (EI/n_h)^(1/5) for a sand top layer; 1.4·R, R = (EI/k_h)^(1/4) otherwise; top-layer n_h / k_h; EI of the casing (micropile) or of the H-pile section about the chosen axis), computed by `computeAll` whether or not Module 10 is enabled. Module 10 measures L_f below the bottom of the unsupported length: L_e = L_u + L_f with L_u = max(L_u input, stickup) measured from the pile head (`colChk`). The graphs plot depth below grade, so the line is at **z = L_u + L_f − s** (s = head height above grade, ft) — the same conversion the Module 10 buckling line already used (`Le_buck − s`). With no unsupported length below grade (L_u = stickup) this is z = L_f, "measured from grade"; otherwise the label and hover say "L_f measured below the bottom of the unsupported length L_u = … ft from the head (Module 10), so … ft below grade".
- **Reference label:** "AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. Art. 10.7.3.13.4 — verify article" (the depth-to-fixity expressions for buckling of piles with an unsupported length, from Davisson & Robinson (1965), are given in the AASHTO pile "Buckling and Lateral Stability" article; the article number is recalled, not checked against the 10th Ed. text, hence "verify", as the tool marks other recalled references). Note: Module 10's own Calc note still says "Not an AASHTO equation"; it is not changed here (UI scope) — see open question in the PR. AASHTO writes the clay form with the soil modulus E_s (= 0.465 s_u, ksi); the tool's 1.4·(EI/k_h)^(1/4) is the same form with its k_h input.
- **Where:**
  - New `LAT_DAV_REF` and `latDavisson(r, s)` before `latKV` (anchor `function latDavisson(r, s) {`): returns the line {k: "dav", z, name, short, lbl, keyVal} from `r.buckling` (null if Module 10 has no value).
  - `latKV` (anchor `const dav = latDavisson(r, s);`): Davisson first in `K.fix` (so it is the primary line); z_fix and 5 % decay follow; the buckling line is added only when `b.enable` and not (`bklTab === "davisson"` without an L_f override) and not at the same depth as the Davisson line.
  - `latOverlay` (F-1): secondary lines 1.0 px (was 1.3), primary 1.8; the primary's on-panel label uses the short form "Davisson z_f x.x ft" (anchor `t: h.short || h.name`).
  - `ElevationPlot` (screen and report F-4): primary (Davisson) labelled below its line at the right; secondary lines 1.0 px at 75 % opacity, their labels stacked at the left of the moment panel with `latStack` (no overlap); without a Davisson value the F26 c placement is unchanged (anchor `if (f.k === "dav") { if (!narrow) anns.push(`). Note text names the teal line.
  - Soil reaction panel (`fixTr`): secondary lines 1.0 px, 75 % opacity.
  - `latKeysFix`: key-strip row "Davisson & Robinson fixity z_f (primary)" with the formula, T or R, datum, "Module 10 value" and the reference (screen strips and printed F-1 / F-4 key tables).

## 2026-10-11 — PR: claude/pile-pmult (PR link added after merge)

Engineer's decisions 2026-10-11 (group p-multipliers): (1) AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. Table 10.7.2.4-1 becomes the default p-multiplier source, the old curve stays selectable as "Rollins / FHWA (legacy curve)" with its exact behaviour; (2) "Apply group p-multipliers automatically (per row)" is a toggle; on, the lateral analysis runs once per row and the governing row drives the checks; (3) "Run all cases" runs every row of every case when the toggle is on.

### F29. Group lateral p-multipliers: AASHTO Table 10.7.2.4-1 by default; optional automatic per-row p-y analysis with the governing row driving the lateral checks   [calc change] [no result change for any saved project or with the toggle off (proven, see How verified). - **Where:**

  - `computeAll`, anchor `// --- 2) Lateral p-multipliers by row`: the inline `pmAt` replaced by `groupPmRows(nRows, s_dia, pmSrc)`; `R.group` gains `pmSource` (normalised), `pmSourceLabel`, `pmBelowTable`, `pmAboveTable`, `pmAuto`, `pmMod`.
  - `DEFAULT_INPUTS`: `groupPmSource: "aashto"` (was `"rollins"`), new `groupPmAuto: false`, `groupPmMod: 1.0`.
  - `mergeSavedInputs`: a project with no `groupPmSource` loads as `"rollins"`.
  - `App`: the `pyRes` memo body became `solvePyResFor(gPM)`; `pyResSingle` (toggle off, `gPM = I.pyPM || 1`, unchanged) and `pyRowsRaw` (toggle on, one solve per row); `rOptsFor(pyRes)` (the old body of the `r` memo, unchanged) and `pyRowsEval` (computeAll per row, governing row); `pyRes` / `r` now come from them. `runAllCases` (anchor `const runOne = (gPMc)`), the `caseRes` / `pcr` reset lists, `computePcr` (`gPM: pcrGPM`).
  - UI: `PmAutoToggle`, `PmRowTable` (before `function GroupPlan(`); Module 02 (after Step 1); `PyPanel` p-multiplier field; Module 11 section "2 · Lateral p-multipliers (f_m) by row" (id `pd-grp-pm`) and its code label; `GroupPlan` caption; `LoadCasesCard` envelope; Lateral graphs card subtitle; Figure F-3 note; report: solver settings, Group inputs, 02 (p-y constants line, per-row table, model setup row), 11 (row values, per-row table), envelope.
- **What changed:**
  1. **Source.** `groupPmRows(nRows, s_dia, src)`; `s_dia` = c/c spacing / bond-hole diameter, as Module 11 always computed it. Row index: leading, 2nd, 3rd and later.
     - `"aashto"` (default for new projects, label "AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. Table 10.7.2.4-1 — verify table number/values"): 3B 0.80 / 0.40 / 0.30, 5B 1.00 / 0.85 / 0.70; linear between 3B and 5B; **the 5B values above 5B**; below 3B the 3B values with an amber warning ("outside the table … may be unconservative").
     - `"rollins"` ("Rollins / FHWA (legacy curve)"): the pre-F29 `pmAt` code, character for character (3B values at or below 3B, linear 3B–5B, ramp from the 5B values to 1.0 at 6B, 1.0 at or above 6B, clamp [0.2, 1.0]); no warning, as before.
     - Module 11 has a source selector (there was none: the saved `groupPmSource` was never read). With the legacy curve a note says it was kept from the saved data and offers "Use AASHTO →".
  2. **Old projects (§5).** Every project saved by main carries `groupPmSource: "rollins"` (main saved its full input set) and keeps it, so it reproduces exactly; a project with no source saved is migrated to `"rollins"` on load (`mergeSavedInputs`). New projects (no saved data, or "reset") start with `"aashto"`. No storage key or format changed; two optional fields were added (`groupPmAuto`, `groupPmMod`); a missing field takes its default (off, 1.0).
  3. **Toggle "Apply group p-multipliers automatically (per row)"** (`I.groupPmAuto`, shown in Module 02 and Module 11). Active only when `groupPmAutoOn(I)`: toggle on **and** Pile group mode (`groupEnable`) **and** built-in p-y **and** not integral abutment. Single-pile mode: shown disabled with "Single pile — enter the p-multiplier directly."; external LPILE / linear basis: disabled with a note.
     - **Definition:** final p-multiplier of row k = row f_m(k) × modifier, modifier = `I.groupPmMod` (default 1.00, shown when the toggle is on). The Module 02 "p-multiplier" field (`pyPM`) is not used while the toggle is on (field disabled, labelled so); it is kept unchanged in the data, so switching the toggle off restores the previous analysis.
     - **Loads:** each row is solved with the active case's per-pile loads (manual cases are per pile; Group ▦ rows carry the design pile's axial and its equal shear share from the rigid-cap distribution, `computeCapDist` `sel.Vres`, unchanged).
     - **Governing row** (`pmPickGov`): largest D/C of the lateral-dependent checks, D/C = max(flexure, combined) exactly as the envelope defines them (micropile M_max/φM_n and the P-M interaction; H-pile M_u/φM_n and the 6.9.2.2 interaction); a row whose solve did not converge (F22/F27 rules, `solvePyWithRetry` unchanged) has D/C = ∞ and governs (lateral checks NG); ties → larger M_max, then the smaller p-multiplier. Each row is evaluated with `computeAll(I, rOptsFor(rowSolve))`, the same options the module result uses, so the governing row's values ARE the module values.
     - The governing row's p-y result becomes `pyRes` → Modules 02 / 04 / 05 / 10 / G, the Lateral graphs (subtitle "governing row k of n (f_m = x.xx)"; Figure F-3 note says the curves are the governing row's) and the report. Per-row table (row, f_m, [p-mult used when modifier ≠ 1], M_max, y₀, flexure D/C, combined D/C, lateral status = flexure, combined, stability, micropile casing extension) in Module 02, Module 11 and the printed 02 and 11 sections.
     - **Compute P_cr** (Module 10 ramp) with the toggle on uses the smallest row p-multiplier (trailing row: least soil support, lowest P_cr). Chosen to keep P_cr independent of the governing-row choice (which itself reads P_cr through the buckling check); off: `pyPM` as before.
  4. **Run all cases:** with the toggle on every case runs every row (same `solvePyWithRetry` call and `computeAll` options as before, `gPM` = row value); the row reported is the governing one by the same rule (service rows: largest |y₀|). Envelope rows say "· row k (f_m x.xx)" (screen) / "· governing row k (f_m = x.xx)" (report), plus a note.
  5. **"Apply avg f_m" button:** kept as a helper when the toggle is off, with two more ("use leading row", "use trailing row"); hidden when the toggle is on (the per-row results show instead). Kept because it is the only route for an engineer who wants one p-multiplier for a single pile check, and old projects used it.
  6. **Toggle default: OFF for new projects too.** The toggle does nothing in single-pile mode (the default mode), and the engineer often checks one pile on its own; turning it on is a deliberate, visible choice saved with the project, so a project never changes its basis because the mode was switched. When Pile group mode is chosen the toggle is right next to the row table (Module 11) and the p-multiplier field (Module 02).
- **Governing provision:** AASHTO LRFD Bridge Design Specifications, 10th Ed. (2024), Art. 10.7.2.4 and Table 10.7.2.4-1 (pile p-multipliers P_m for multiple-row shading; values above as given by the engineer — **verify the table number and values against the 10th Ed.**). Legacy curve: Rollins et al. / Reese & Van Impe / FHWA GEC-10 style (as before).
- **§4 callouts:**
  - **(a) Source change at the defaults and for old projects.** Before: every project used the Rollins curve (`groupPmSource` was saved but never read). After: new projects use AASHTO; saved projects keep their saved source ("rollins" from every main save; a file with none → "rollins"). Between 3B and 5B and below 3B both sources give the same numbers. Worked check, defaults (3 × 3 group at 3.0 × bond dia, s = 21 in, d_h = 7 in): before 0.80 / 0.40 / 0.30 (avg 0.50); after 0.80 / 0.40 / 0.30 (avg 0.50) — identical. Effect on results with the toggle off: none (the row values only display and feed the helper buttons).
  - **(b) Spacing above 5B.** 2 columns × 3 rows at s = 5.5 × bond dia (micropile, s = 38.5 in, d_h = 7 in). Before (legacy): f = f5 + (1 − f5)(5.5 − 5)/1 → row 1: 1.0 + 0 = **1.000**; row 2: 0.85 + 0.15 × 0.5 = **0.925**; row 3: 0.70 + 0.30 × 0.5 = **0.850** (avg 0.925). After (AASHTO): the 5B values **1.00 / 0.85 / 0.70** (avg 0.85). Rows 2 and 3+ lower → **more conservative** (less soil resistance). Verified in the app: legacy project at 5.5B shows 1 / 0.925 / 0.85 on main and on the branch; AASHTO project shows 1 / 0.85 / 0.70. With the toggle on (case Manual Str, STL 80 kip, V 3 kip, micropile defaults): rows M_max 20.28 / 21.33 / **22.79** kip·ft, governing row 3 (f_m 0.70), flexure D/C 0.422, combined 0.580; H-pile 16.94 / 17.27 / **17.67** kip·ft, governing row 3, D/C 0.033 / 0.077.
  - **(c) Spacing below 3B.** AASHTO: 3B values used (same numbers as the legacy curve, which also used the 3B values) plus an amber warning in Module 11 and a line in report 11: "Spacing 2.50× is below 3B — outside the table. The 3B values are used; closer spacing has more shadowing, so they may be unconservative." Check: s = 2.5 × d_h → 0.80 / 0.40 / 0.30 before and after; no result change.
  - **(d) Automatic per row vs the old "avg f_m".** 2 × 3 group, 3 rows at 3B (f_m 0.80 / 0.40 / 0.30, avg 0.50), default soil (sand γ 120 pcf, φ 32°, k 90 pci), free head, stickup 3 ft, case "Manual Str" STL = 80 kip, V = 3 kip per pile, M_head = 0. Old method: p-multiplier field = avg 0.50 applied to the one pile. New: three solves.

    | Pile | Row (f_m) | M_max (kip·ft) | y₀ (in) | flexure D/C | combined D/C | lateral |
    |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
    | Micropile (7.0 in casing) | 1 (0.80) | 21.77 | 1.131 | 0.404 | 0.561 | OK |
    | | 2 (0.40) | 28.99 | 1.987 | 0.537 | 0.695 | OK |
    | | **3 (0.30) governs** | **34.30** | **2.707** | **0.636** | **0.793** | **NG** (casing extension: tip 12.0 ft < M→5 % depth 12.6 ft) |

    | H-pile (defaults) | 1 (0.80) | 17.40 | 0.0912 | 0.0323 | 0.0766 | OK |

The leading row alone (f_m 0.80) is **less conservative** than the average (micropile 21.77 vs 26.08). With modifier 0.90 the micropile governing row uses 0.27: M_max 37.02 kip·ft, y₀ 3.106 in. At V = 6 kip (micropile) rows 2 and 3 did not converge → governing row 3, "did not converge", lateral checks NG (row 1 alone: M_max 56.98, flexure D/C 1.056).
- **Pure refactor parts (no result change claimed):** `groupPmRows(…, "rollins")` is the old `pmAt` body; `rOptsFor` is the old `r` memo body; `solvePyResFor(I.pyPM || 1)` is the old `pyRes` memo body (its four `I.pyPM || 1` became `gPM`). +/* ============================================================
+   GROUP LATERAL p-MULTIPLIERS BY ROW (F29, 2026-10-11)
+   ------------------------------------------------------------
+   Row f_m for the leading row, the 2nd row and the 3rd and later rows, from the
+   c/c spacing in diameters s_dia (s / bond-hole diameter, as Module 11 computes it).
+   Sources (I.groupPmSource):

+   and meaningful (pile group mode, built-in p-y, not integral abutment). The App then
+   runs the p-y solve once per row with p-multiplier = row f_m x I.groupPmMod.
+============================================================ */
+const GROUP_PM_SRC_LABEL = { aashto: "AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. Table 10.7.2.4-1 — verify table number/values", rollins: "Rollins / FHWA (legacy curve)" };
+function groupPmSourceOf(I) { return (I && I.groupPmSource === "rollins") ? "rollins" : "aashto"; }
+function groupPmRows(nRows, s_dia, src) {
+  const pmAt = (rowIdx) => {
+    // anchor tables: [leading, second, third+]
+    const at3 = [0.8, 0.4, 0.3];
+    const at5 = [1.0, 0.85, 0.7];
+    const pick = (arr)=> arr[Math.min(rowIdx,2)];
+    const f3 = pick(at3), f5 = pick(at5);
+    let fm;
+    if (src === "rollins") {
+      // legacy curve (Rollins, Reese & Van Impe; FHWA GEC-10 style), exactly as before F29
+      if (s_dia <= 3) fm = f3;
+      else if (s_dia >= 6) fm = 1.0;         // essentially isolated at >=6D
+      else if (s_dia >= 5) fm = f5 + (1.0 - f5)*((s_dia-5)/1);
+      else fm = f3 + (f5 - f3)*((s_dia-3)/2); // interpolate 3D->5D
+      return Math.max(Math.min(fm,1.0),0.2);
+    }
+    // AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. Table 10.7.2.4-1
+    if (s_dia <= 3) fm = f3;                 // below 3B: outside the table, 3B values (warned)
+    else if (s_dia >= 5) fm = f5;            // at and above 5B: the 5B values
+    else fm = f3 + (f5 - f3)*((s_dia-3)/2);  // linear 3B -> 5B
+    return fm;
+  };
+  return Array.from({length:nRows}, (_,i)=>({ row:i+1, fm: pmAt(i) }));
+}
+function groupPmTable(I) {
+  const nRows = Math.max(1, Math.round(I.groupNrows||1));
+  const dh_in = bondHoleDia(I);
+  const s_in = (I.groupSpacingIn && I.groupSpacingIn>0) ? I.groupSpacingIn : (I.groupSpacingDia||3)*dh_in;
+  const s_dia = s_in/Math.max(dh_in,1e-6);
+  const src = groupPmSourceOf(I);
+  const rows = groupPmRows(nRows, s_dia, src);
+  return { src, srcLabel: GROUP_PM_SRC_LABEL[src], nRows, s_in, s_dia, rows,
+    avg: rows.reduce((a,b)=>a+b.fm,0)/nRows, belowTable: s_dia < 3 - 1e-9, aboveTable: s_dia > 5 + 1e-9 };
+}
+function groupPmModOf(I) { const v = +(I && I.groupPmMod); return (isFinite(v) && v > 0) ? v : 1.0; }
+function groupPmAutoOn(I) { return !!(I && I.groupPmAuto && I.groupEnable && I.lateralSource === "py" && I.pileType !== "iab"); }
+// One row's lateral-dependent results (from computeAll R and the row's p-y result pr):
+// D/C as the case envelope reports them (micropile: M_max / phi M_n and the P-M interaction;
+// H-pile: Mu / phi Mn and the 6.9.2.2 interaction), and the lateral checks' status (flexure,
+// combined, casing extension (micropile), stability). A row with no valid solve is NG.
+function pmRowSummary(R, pr, I) {
+  const nc = !(pr && pr.ok);
+  const hs = R.hpileStruct, isHP = I.pileType === "hpile" && R.hpileGeo && hs;
+  const flexR = nc ? null : (isHP ? (hs.phiMn > 0 ? hs.Mu / hs.phiMn : null) : (R.flex.phiMn > 0 ? R.MmaxUsed / R.flex.phiMn : null));
+  const combR = nc ? null : (isHP ? hs.comb_ratio : R.comb.interaction);
+  const latPass = !nc && (isHP ? (hs.flex_pass && hs.comb_pass2 !== false) : (R.flex.pass && R.comb.pass && R.casingExt.pass)) && !!(R.stability && R.stability.pass);
+  const dc = nc ? Infinity : Math.max(isFinite(flexR) ? flexR : 0, isFinite(combR) ? combR : 0);
+  return { noConv: nc, flexR, combR, latPass, dc, Mmax: nc ? null : pr.Mmax_kft, y0: nc ? null : pr.headDefl_in };
+}
+// Governing row: the largest dc (a row that did not converge has dc = Infinity and governs);
+// ties (within 1e-9) -> the larger Mmax, then the smaller p-multiplier (less soil support).
+function pmPickGov(ev) {
+  let g = 0;
+  for (let k = 1; k < ev.length; k++) {
+    const a = ev[k], b = ev[g];
+    const tie = (x, y) => (x === y) || (isFinite(x) && isFinite(y) && Math.abs(x - y) <= 1e-9 * Math.max(1, Math.abs(x), Math.abs(y)));
+    if (a.dc > b.dc && !tie(a.dc, b.dc)) { g = k; continue; }
+    if (!tie(a.dc, b.dc)) continue;
+    const am = a.Mmax == null ? -1 : a.Mmax, bm = b.Mmax == null ? -1 : b.Mmax;
+    if (am > bm && !tie(am, bm)) { g = k; continue; }
+    if (tie(am, bm) && a.pm < b.pm) g = k;
+  }
+  return g;
+}
 function bondHoleDia(I) {
   return (I.dhBondSeparate && isFinite(I.dhBond) && I.dhBond > 0) ? I.dhBond : I.OD;
 }

## 2026-10-11 — PR: claude/pile-o41 (PR link added after merge)

Engineer's decision 2026-10-11 (O41): the group spacing ratio s/B for the p-multipliers (AASHTO and legacy) and for the axial group efficiency η uses B = the pile width the p-y analysis uses for that pile type. Micropile unchanged.

### F30. H-pile groups: s/B, η, Converse-Labarre θ and the block footprint use the H-pile p-y width B, and the c/c spacing the group workspace uses (O41)   [calc change] [H-pile groups only; micropile and integral-abutment results bit-identical (proven). MORE conservative for strong-axis H-piles at the default spacing (η 1.00 → 0.747) and wherever the spacing is entered in inches (s/B smaller → lower row f_m, lower η); LESS conservative for the block-failure perimeter (larger footprint) and for weak-axis H-piles at a spacing in diameters (s/B 3.00 → 3.19, row f_m up). See the check cases]

- **Where:**
  - New top-level helpers after `function bondHoleDia(I) {`: `groupB(I)`, `groupCcSpacing(I)`, `groupBLabel(I)`.
  - `groupPmTable` (anchor `const dh_in = groupB(I);`): B and s from the helpers; returns `Blbl`.
  - `computeAll`, group block (anchor `// F30 (O41): B = the p-y width`): `dh_in = groupB(I)`, `s_in = groupCcSpacing(I)`; `R.group` gains `Blbl`.
  - `GroupWorkspaceBody` `genGrid` (anchor `const s = g.s_in / 12;`).
  - Text: Module 11 header line (`spacing = " + fmt(r.group.s_dia, 1) + "× " + r.group.Blbl`), section 1 spacing notes (✓/⚠, θ = atan(B/s) for H-piles), Group options panel η note, `GroupPlan` caption (`s = x.xB` for H-piles), report 11 p-multiplier line, `PmRowTable` note (`info.Blbl`, added in the `pyRowsEval` memo).
- **Problem:** `computeAll` and `groupPmTable` took B = `bondHoleDia(I)` (micropile casing OD unless d_h is entered) for every pile type, and the spacing given in diameters as `groupSpacingDia × bondHoleDia(I)`. In H-pile mode both used the micropile OD input (7 in by default), not the H-pile. The group workspace, the Group ▦ case loads (`groupGeom`, `groupGeomLocal`, the bootstrap centroid) space the piles at `groupSpacingDia × pileWidth(I)`, so in H-pile mode Module 11 also showed a different layout (and per-pile forces) from the one the cases used. Example, defaults: Module 11 / report 11 said 21 in c/c and 80.0 kip on pile 1; the Group ▦ case used 41.49 in c/c and 178.8 kip.
- **Before:**

```js
// groupPmTable
  const dh_in = bondHoleDia(I);
  const s_in = (I.groupSpacingIn && I.groupSpacingIn>0) ? I.groupSpacingIn : (I.groupSpacingDia||3)*dh_in;
  const s_dia = s_in/Math.max(dh_in,1e-6);
// computeAll
  const dh_in = dh;                                          // bond/drilled-hole dia (in)
  const s_in = (I.groupSpacingIn && I.groupSpacingIn>0) ? I.groupSpacingIn : (I.groupSpacingDia||3)*dh_in;
// genGrid
    const s = (I.groupSpacingIn && I.groupSpacingIn > 0 ? I.groupSpacingIn : (I.groupSpacingDia || 3) * (g.dh_in)) / 12;
```

- **After:**

```js
function groupB(I) {
  if (I.pileType === "hpile") return I.hpAxis === "weak" ? I.hpD : I.hpBf;
  return bondHoleDia(I);
}
function groupCcSpacing(I) {
  if (I.groupSpacingIn && I.groupSpacingIn > 0) return I.groupSpacingIn;
  return (I.groupSpacingDia || 3) * (I.pileType === "hpile" ? pileWidth(I) : bondHoleDia(I));
}
function groupBLabel(I) { return I.pileType === "hpile" ? "B" : "bond dia"; }
// groupPmTable / computeAll
  const dh_in = groupB(I);
  const s_in = groupCcSpacing(I);
  const s_dia = s_in/Math.max(dh_in,1e-6);
// genGrid
    const s = g.s_in / 12;
```

- **What changed (H-pile mode only):**
  1. **B** = the width `buildPySetup` gives the p-y springs: b_f for strong-axis bending, d for weak-axis bending (`I.hpBf` / `I.hpD`, the projected width normal to the load). Note: this is **not** `pileWidth(I)`, which is the section dimension in the bending plane (d strong / b_f weak, used for the head-fixity screen and the drawings). B drives s/B (row f_m, AASHTO and legacy; the below-3B / above-5B notes), the η threshold s/B ≥ 3, Converse-Labarre θ = atan(B/s) and the block footprint (n−1)·s + B in both directions.
  2. **s** (spacing given in diameters) = `groupSpacingDia × pileWidth(I)`, the spacing the group workspace, the Group ▦ case loads and the plan already used. Module 11's rigid-cap distribution table, plan and derivation, report 11 and the 3D view now show that layout (display only: the checks already ran on the case loads from that layout). An explicit spacing in inches is used as entered (unchanged).
  3. **"Generate grid"** in the workspace writes the grid at `R.group.s_in` (H-pile: the workspace spacing above, was × OD; micropile: the same expression as before).
  4. **Labels:** H-pile text says "× B" and "B = 14.70 in (H-pile b_f, strong-axis bending: the p-y width normal to the load)"; micropile text unchanged ("× bond dia").
  - Not changed: the micropile (B = bond-hole diameter, s = × bond-hole diameter) and the integral-abutment path; the axial efficiency and block checks still reduce the micropile bond capacity `R.geo.Pn_geo` in H-pile mode too (new open item O43); the plan symbol size in `GroupPlanSvg` (`pileWidth`).
- **Governing provision:** AASHTO LRFD Bridge Design Specifications, 10th Ed. (2024), Art. 10.7.2.4 and Table 10.7.2.4-1 (P_m by row as a function of c/c spacing in pile diameters / widths B — verify the table number and values, as F29). η: FHWA NHI-05-039 (spacing ≥ 3 × diameter → η = 1.0) and the Converse-Labarre formula, as before. No formula, factor or table value changed; only the B and s fed to them in H-pile mode.
- **§4 callouts (worked checks).** 2 columns × 3 rows, HP 14×89 defaults (d 13.83 in, b_f 14.70 in, strong axis → B = 14.70 in, pileWidth = 13.83 in), source AASHTO, "Apply group p-multipliers automatically" on, case Manual Str (STL 80 kip, V 3 kip per pile, M 0), default soil (sand γ 120 pcf, φ 32°, k 90 pci), micropile bond inputs at the defaults (R.geo.Pn_geo = 109.96 kip, β 2.50 ksf, L_b 24 ft, φ_geo 0.70).
  - **(a) Default spacing, 3.0 × dia.**

    | | Before | After |
    |---|---|---|
    | s (in) | 3 × 7.00 (OD) = 21.00 | 3 × 13.83 (d) = 41.49 |
    | B (in) | 7.00 (OD) | 14.70 (b_f) |
    | s/B | 3.000 | 41.49 / 14.70 = **2.822** (< 3B: amber note, 3B values) |
    | f_m rows 1 / 2 / 3 | 0.80 / 0.40 / 0.30 | 0.80 / 0.40 / 0.30 (no change) |
    | Per-row M_max (kip·ft) / y₀ (in) | 17.40 / 0.0912; 19.12 / 0.1315; **20.61 / 0.1629** (row 3 governs) | identical |

## 2026-10-11 — PR: claude/pile-group3 (PR link added after merge)

Engineer's decisions 2026-10-11 (O42, O43 and the H-pile "spacing × dia"): "yes go ahead with all three, only when group is used." All three apply only in Pile group mode (`groupEnable` on); single-pile results are bit-identical (proven, see How verified). F33 applies only with "Apply group p-multipliers automatically (per row)" on.

### F31. H-pile groups: "spacing × dia" means × B (the p-y width normal to the load), in the workspace, the Group ▦ case loads and Module 11; η threshold with a round-off tolerance   [calc change] [H-pile groups with the spacing given in diameters only; micropile, integral abutment, explicit spacing in inches and single piles bit-identical (proven). Strong axis: piles 6.3 % farther apart → per-pile axial from cap moments lower on the far piles / higher on the near ones (LESS or MORE conservative per pile: in the check case the governing pile's axial goes up, 178.8 → 184.8 kip, MORE conservative); η at exactly 3B 0.747 → 1.000 (LESS conservative); block footprint larger (LESS conservative). Weak axis: s/B 3.19 → 3.00 → row f_m and η lower (MORE conservative)]

- **Where:**
  - New top-level `groupWsSpacing(I)` after `groupCcSpacing` (anchor `function groupWsSpacing(I) {`).
  - `groupCcSpacing` (anchor `return (I.groupSpacingDia || 3) * (I.pileType === "hpile" ? groupB(I) : bondHoleDia(I));`): H-pile width `pileWidth(I)` → `groupB(I)`.
  - The four workspace / case-load layouts that spaced the grid at `groupSpacingDia × pileWidth(I)`: `GroupLayoutView` (`const geom = …`), `GroupCasesTable` (`const geom = …`), `GroupWorkspaceBody` (`const groupGeomLocal = …`), `App` (`const groupGeom = …`, used by the Group ▦ case rows); and the hand-off bootstrap `centroid(I)` (anchor `var g={nRows:I.groupNrows,nCols:I.groupNcols,s_in:`), all now `groupWsSpacing(I)`.
  - `App` `groupCasesEmitted` memo dependency list: `I.pileType, I.hpAxis, I.hpBf, I.hpD` added.
  - `computeAll` η threshold (anchor `const spacingOKforEta = s_dia >= spacingThreshDia - 1e-9;`).
  - Text: workspace label "spacing ×B" (H-pile) with a tooltip giving B; report Group inputs row "Spacing (diameters) … ×B, B = 14.70 in (H-pile p-y width)".
- **Problem:** (1) In H-pile mode the workspace, the plan and the Group ▦ case loads spaced a grid given in diameters at `groupSpacingDia × pileWidth(I)` = × d (strong axis) or × b_f (weak axis), the section dimension in the bending plane. F30 made Module 11's s/B use B = the p-y width normal to the load (b_f strong, d weak), so "3 × dia" was 41.49 / 14.70 = 2.82B strong axis (below the AASHTO table, amber note, η reduced) and 44.10 / 13.83 = 3.19B weak axis. Engineer: "spacing × dia" for an H-pile means × B. (2) The η threshold test `s/B ≥ 3` had no tolerance: 3 × 14.70 / 14.70 = 2.9999999999999996 in floating point, so a spacing entered as exactly 3B would still get the Converse-Labarre reduction. (3) Found while checking: the Group ▦ case-load memo did not list the pile type or the H-pile dimensions among its dependencies, so after switching Micropile → H-pile (or changing b_f / d / the axis) the Group ▦ rows kept the old layout's loads until another group input changed. A project opened in H-pile mode was not affected.

- **What changed (H-pile, spacing in diameters):** the c/c spacing is `groupSpacingDia × B` (B = `groupB(I)`: b_f strong axis, d weak axis) everywhere: Module 11 (s/B, f_m, η, θ, block footprint, rigid-cap table), "Generate grid" (writes `R.group.s_in`), the plan, the Group ▦ case loads (per-pile axial / shear from `computeCapDist`), the Loads & group per-pile table and the foundation-load import's default load location (group centroid). So "3 × dia" is exactly 3.00B. Micropile: `groupWsSpacing` = `groupSpacingDia × pileWidth(I)` = × casing OD and `groupCcSpacing` = × bond-hole diameter, exactly as before (O44 still open). Spacing entered in inches: used as entered (unchanged).
- **Governing provision:** AASHTO LRFD Bridge Design Specifications, 10th Ed. (2024), Art. 10.7.2.4 and Table 10.7.2.4-1 (P_m by row vs c/c spacing in pile widths B — verify table number and values, as F29); FHWA NHI-05-039 (η = 1.0 at spacing ≥ 3 × diameter) and the Converse-Labarre formula, as before. No formula, factor or table value changed: only the spacing the H-pile layout uses, and the round-off tolerance (1e-9, the same as the p-multiplier table's 3B / 5B tests) on the η threshold.
- **§4 callouts (worked checks).** 2 columns × 3 rows, HP 14×89 defaults (d 13.83 in, b_f 14.70 in), spacing "3 × dia", source AASHTO, "Apply group p-multipliers automatically" on, cases Manual Str (STL 80 kip, V 3 kip per pile, M 0), Svc I, Manual EE, Group ▦ Str I (cap P 480 kip, V_x 18 kip at (0.875, 1.75) ft) and Group ▦ Ext I (P 360, V_x 24), default soil (sand γ 120 pcf, φ 32°, k 90 pci), micropile bond inputs at the defaults (the η / block checks still use them in F31; F32 changes that). ### F32. H-pile groups: the group efficiency check uses the H-pile static resistance; the block check is "not computed — verify by hand" (O43)   [calc change] [H-pile groups only; micropile, integral abutment and single piles bit-identical (proven). The η check is now against the H-pile φR_n (Module 01) instead of the micropile bond: MORE or LESS conservative depending on which is larger (defaults: H-pile φR_n = 0 with no N60 entered → NG either way; sand N60 = 20: 84.88 vs 76.97 kip → LESS conservative, NG → OK). The block check no longer enters the H-pile overall result or the Module 11 status: LESS conservative (a check that failed on the wrong basis is removed; the engineer must verify block failure by hand)]

- **Where:**
  - `computeAll`, after `R.hpileGeo = { … }` (anchor `// ---- F32 (O43, 2026-10-11): H-pile group axial checks on the H-pile capacity ----`): overwrites the `R.group` capacity fields in H-pile mode.
  - `computeAll` H-pile `R.allPass` (anchor `(!grpOn || R.group.geoGroup_pass)`).
  - `grpRows` (check strip "Group block" row: skipped when `blockComputed === false`).
  - Module 11 status (anchor `(r.group.blockComputed === false || r.group.block_pass)`), section 1 heading / text / η line / check row, section 3 (amber "Not computed for H-piles — verify by hand" box).
- **Problem:** in H-pile mode the group efficiency check reduced the **micropile** grout-to-ground bond capacity `R.geo.Pn_geo` (β, d_h, L_b, φ_geo micropile inputs; 109.96 kip at the defaults) and the block check used that bond on the block perimeter over the micropile bond length; both entered the H-pile `allPass` and the Module 11 status. Neither is the H-pile's capacity (F30 open item O43).
- **Before (H-pile and micropile alike):**

```js
  const Pn_geo_group = R.geo.Pn_geo * eta;                  // per-pile bond reduced by eta
  const phiPn_geo_group = phi_geo * Pn_geo_group;
  const geoGroup_pass = !grpOn || phiPn_geo_group >= STL;
  ...
  const Pn_block_side = blockPerim_in * beta_ksi*12 * Lb_block; // kip
  const sumIndiv = R.geo.Pn_geo * nPiles;
  const Pn_block = Pn_block_side;          // (base bearing conservatively neglected)
  const groupBondCap = Math.min(Pn_block, sumIndiv*eta);
  const phiGroupBond = phi_geo*groupBondCap;
  const block_pass = !grpOn || phiGroupBond >= groupDemand;
  ...
    R.allPass = (R.hpileGeo ? R.hpileGeo.pass : false) && structPass && fixPass && R.stability.pass && (!grpOn || (geoGroup_pass && block_pass));
```

- **After (micropile unchanged; H-pile, after `R.hpileGeo`):**

```js
    if (R.group) {
      const g = R.group;
      g.capBasis = "hpile";
      g.Pn_geo_single = geo.Rn_comp;                 // nominal R_n (skin + tip), kip
      g.phiRn_single = geo.phiRn_comp;               // phi R_n, kip
      g.Pn_geo_group = geo.Rn_comp * g.eta;
      g.phiPn_geo_group = geo.phiRn_comp * g.eta;
      g.geoGroup_pass = !grpOn || g.phiPn_geo_group >= STL;
      g.blockComputed = false;
      g.Pn_block = null; g.blockGoverns = null; g.groupBondCap = null; g.phiGroupBond = null; g.block_pass = null;
      g.sumIndiv = geo.Rn_comp * nPiles;
    }
  ...
    R.allPass = (R.hpileGeo ? R.hpileGeo.pass : false) && structPass && fixPass && R.stability.pass && (!grpOn || R.group.geoGroup_pass);
// Module 11 status

// grpRows
  if (r.group.block_pass !== undefined && r.group.blockComputed !== false) out.push(["Group block", …]);
```

- **Efficiency check (H-pile):** η × φR_n ≥ STL, φR_n = the Module 01 static resistance (Σ φ_stat · R_s per layer + φ_stat · R_p, including the small-group 0.80 factor when that option is on). η itself is unchanged (FHWA spacing ≥ 3B → 1.0, else Converse-Labarre on s/B per F30 / F31). The AASHTO 10.7.3.9 group factors for driven piles (cohesionless: η = 1.0; cohesive: 0.65–1.0 by spacing and cap contact) are **not** applied — new open item O45.
- **Block check (H-pile): not computed.** The tool's block mechanism is grout-to-ground bond on the block perimeter over the bond length (base neglected), a micropile model. The driven-pile equivalent (AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. Art. 10.7.3.9: block of soil bounded by the piles in cohesive soil, S̄_u over the block perimeter × embedded length plus N_c·S_u over the base, with its own resistance factor φ_g; FHWA GEC-12 the same) needs a block resistance factor that is not an H-pile input, and for cohesionless layers the tool has no block basis. So Module 11 shows an amber box "Not computed for H-piles — verify by hand" (with the footprint, Σ individual R_n and the factored group demand for reference), and the block is excluded from the H-pile overall result, the Module 11 status and the check strip, rather than showing a wrong number. Micropile block unchanged.
- **Governing provision:** AASHTO LRFD Bridge Design Specifications, 10th Ed. (2024): Art. 10.7.3.8.6 (static H-pile resistance, Module 01, unchanged), Art. 10.7.3.9 (pile group resistance and block failure — referenced, not implemented), Table 10.5.5.2.3-1 (φ_stat, unchanged). FHWA NHI-05-039 / Converse-Labarre for η, as before.
- **§4 callouts (worked checks).** 2 columns × 3 rows, HP 14×89 strong axis, "3 × dia" = 3B (after F31: s = 44.10 in, η = 1.000), toggle on, case Manual Str (STL 80 kip, V 3 kip per pile), micropile bond inputs at the defaults (R.geo.Pn_geo = 109.96 kip, φ_geo 0.70, β 2.50 ksf, L_b 24 ft), embedded length 30 ft below grade, stickup 3 ft.
  - **(a) Default soil (sand, no N60 entered → H-pile R_s = R_p = 0; Module 01 already NG).**

    | | Before (F31) | After (F32) |
    |---|---|---|
    | per-pile capacity used | micropile bond P_n = 109.96, φ = 0.70 | H-pile R_n = 0, φR_n = 0 |
    | η check | 0.70 × 1.000 × 109.96 = 76.97 < 80 **NG** | 1.000 × 0 = 0 < 80 **NG** |
    | block | 0.70 × min(1617.0, 659.8) = 461.8 < 480 **NG** | not computed — verify by hand |
    | Module 11 / overall | NG / NG | NG / NG (Module 01 and η) |

  - **(b) Sand with N60 = 20 (same γ, φ, k).** Hand check of Module 01 (unchanged): box perimeter 2(13.83 + 14.70)/12 = 4.755 ft, box area 13.83 × 14.70/144 = 1.4118 ft²; q_s = N60/50 = 0.40 ksf → R_s = 0.40 × 4.755 × 30 = 57.06 kip; q_p = min(0.8 × 20 × 30/1.225, 8 × 20) = min(391.8, 160) = 160 ksf → R_p = 160 × 1.4118 = 225.89 kip; R_n = 282.95 kip; φR_n = 0.30 × 282.95 = **84.89 kip** (φ_stat sand 0.30).

    | | Before (F31) | After (F32) |
    |---|---|---|
    | η check | 0.70 × 1.000 × 109.96 = 76.97 < 80 **NG** | 1.000 × 84.89 = **84.89 ≥ 80 OK** |
    | block | 461.8 < 480 **NG** | not computed — verify by hand (Σ individual R_n = 6 × 282.95 = 1697.7 kip shown for reference; factored demand 480 kip) |
    | Module 11 status | NG | **OK** |
    | Overall (active case Manual Str) / envelope Manual Str | NG / ✗ | **OK / ✓** |
    | Group ▦ Str I / Ext I (STL 184.8 / 138.6 kip > φR_n 84.9) | ✗ | ✗ (Module 01 governs) |

    **LESS conservative** here (the micropile bond was lower than the H-pile resistance, and the block no longer fails the group); in a profile where φR_n < 0.70 × P_n,bond it is MORE conservative.
  - **(c) Weak axis, N60 = 20, and toggle off:** the same η-check numbers (R_n uses max(d, b_f) for the tip width, unchanged); lateral results unchanged by F32.
- **Pure refactor parts:** none in the micropile path; micropile `R.group` and every micropile result unchanged (verified bit-identical).
- **How verified:**
  - `node --check` on the four inline scripts.
  - Headless Chromium (pinned libraries served locally), F31 commit vs this commit, same procedure as F31 (load, "Run all cases", every case active in turn, envelope re-run):
    - **Bit-identical (0 numeric, 0 text differences):** micropile group, default soil and sand N60 = 20.
    - **H-pile groups** (strong axis at the defaults and with N60 = 20, weak axis with N60 = 20, toggle off with N60 = 20): differences only in `R.group` (`Pn_geo_single`, `phiRn_single`, `Pn_geo_group`, `phiPn_geo_group`, `geoGroup_pass`, `capBasis`, `blockComputed`, block fields null, `sumIndiv`) and what follows from them: Module 11 status, check strip "1 check not satisfied" → "All checks OK", envelope Manual Str ✗ → ✓ (N60 = 20, numbers in (b)); lateral results identical.
  - Single-pile H-pile: displayed values identical (the H-pile `R.group` internals are unused when the group is off). Integral abutment: identical.
  - Screenshot looked at: Module 11, H-pile group, N60 = 20 (η line "per-pile H-pile φR_n = 84.9 kip (R_n = 283.0 kip) → ηφR_n = 84.9 kip", check row, amber block box). No console errors.
- **Other copies:** none.

```

### F33. Per-row group analysis: the cap's lateral load is shared between the rows for equal head deflection (rigid cap), each row checked with its own shear (O42)   [calc change] [only with "Apply group p-multipliers automatically (per row)" on in Pile group mode; toggle off, single pile, integral abutment bit-identical (proven). The leading row now takes more shear than the equal share (≈ 42–43 % of the cap shear for 3 rows at 3B vs 33 %) and the trailing rows less. H-pile check case: governing row 3 → row 1, M_max 20.61 → 22.47 kip·ft (MORE conservative). Micropile check case: governing row 3 → row 1, M_max 34.30 → 30.61 kip·ft (LESS conservative for M_max), the trailing row's casing-extension NG still makes the result NG. See the check cases]

- **Where:**
  - New top-level `eqDeflDistribute` (with `EQD_TOL_REL`, `EQD_TOL_ABS`, `EQD_MAX_IT`) and `pyHeadV` before `function bondHoleDia(I) {`.
  - `pmRowSummary`: returns `ngParts` (names of the row's failing lateral-dependent checks; H-pile also shear) and `shearOK` (display / overall result).
  - `App`: `solvePyResFor(gPM, Vov)` (optional head shear; omitted = `I.Plat`, unchanged); `pyRowsRaw` (anchor `// F33 (O42): rigid-cap equal-deflection distribution`), its dependency list (`I.groupNcols` added); `rOptsFor(pyRes, Iv = I)` (`I.Plat` → `Iv.Plat` in the deflection-matched L_f); `pyRowsEval` (rows checked with `Plat = V_k`; `info.eq`, `info.govV`, row `n / V / share / ngParts`; `otherNG`).
  - `runAllCases`: `caseSolve(gPMc, Vc)` split out of `runOne`; `runOne(gPMc, Vc = c.Plat, solPre = null)`; the per-row branch (anchor `// F33 (O42): rigid-cap equal-deflection distribution of the case's lateral load over the`); service ranking; `pass` = every row passes.
  - Display: `PmRowTable` (n piles, V per pile, share, y₀ = y_cap columns, title, note, red "other row NG" line); envelope labels (screen and report: "· row k (f_m x.xx, V x.xx)") and notes; Lateral graphs pushover "design point" and its key-value strip (`pyHeadV`); report 02 "Lateral load applied (governing row k)"; report H-pile section "Lateral / moment".
- **Problem:** with the per-row toggle on (F29) every row was solved with the same per-pile shear (the rigid-cap equal share). A rigid cap forces all pile heads to the same lateral deflection, so the stiffer leading row attracts more of the cap shear and the shadowed trailing rows less (O42). Equal shares understate the leading row's demand and overstate the trailing rows'.
- **Method (engineer's decision 2026-10-11):** find the common head deflection y_cap with Σ_rows n_r · V_r(y_cap) = V_total, V_r(y) = the head shear of one pile of row r (p-multiplier = row f_m × modifier) at head deflection y from the nonlinear p-y solve with the case's axial load, head moment and head condition.
  - The solver is load-controlled (no prescribed head deflection), so the iteration is on the row shears: a multi-row secant iteration (`eqDeflDistribute`). Each row is linearised y₀,r ≈ y_r + s_r (V − V_r), s_r = dy₀/dV through the row's two latest solves (first step: the secant through the origin y_r / V_r, or a probe solve at V + max(0.25 V, 0.5 kip) when V = 0). The linear system gives y* = [V_total − Σ n_r V_r + Σ n_r y_r / s_r] / Σ (n_r / s_r) and V_r ← V_r + (y* − y_r) / s_r, which meets Σ n_r V_r = V_total exactly; every row is re-solved with `solvePyWithRetry` (the same call and acceptance tests as before, F22 / F25 / F27).
  - **Start:** the equal-share solves (the pre-F33 row results), so the first iterate is the F29 answer. A row whose equal-share solve did not converge starts at half that load (up to 4 halvings).
  - **Converged** when Σ n_r V_r = V_total (to 1e-9 relative) and every row's y₀ is within **0.05 % of y_cap (or 1e-5 in, the larger)** of y_cap = Σ n_r y₀,r / Σ n_r. At most 25 iterations.
  - **Non-convergence:** a trial load at which a row's solve does not converge is halved back toward the row's last converged load twice; if it still fails (or needs halving in 3 iterations running), that row is "did not converge" at the shear it needs (F22 rules: dc = ∞, it governs, lateral checks NG, Module 02 shows the reason "equal-deflection distribution: row k did not converge at the shear it needs (x kip per pile)"). If the iteration itself does not converge in 25 iterations, every row is "did not converge" (NG).
  - **Loads:** V_total = n × the case's per-pile lateral load (manual cases: the per-pile value; Group ▦ rows: the design pile's resultant shear `Vres`, as the case already carried); n_r = `groupNcols` piles per row (`groupNrows` rows, row 1 leading). **Biaxial:** the tool already reduces a biaxial cap shear to one per-pile resultant (`Vres` = √((V_x/n)² + (V_y/n)²), the same on every pile); that resultant is distributed over the rows as one load along the row direction (O47). **Head moment:** the case's per-pile head moment on every row (the tool's existing per-pile rule; free head / rotational spring only, as before). **Axial:** the case's per-pile axial on every row (unchanged).
  - **Checks:** each row is checked with its own shear (`computeAll` with Plat = V_r: H-pile shear 6.10.9 uses it; the deflection-matched equivalent cantilever L_f uses V_r); governing row = largest flexure / combined D/C (F29 rule, unchanged). New: a row other than the governing one whose lateral-dependent checks (or H-pile shear) fail makes the overall result NG (`allPass` false, envelope ✗), and the per-row table names it (e.g. "✗ Row 3: casing extension NG — not the governing row …"). Without this the result could read OK while the trailing row fails casing extension (open item O46 asks whether that row should govern instead).
  - **Run all cases:** with the toggle on every case is distributed the same way (`eqDeflDistribute` with the case's loads, same start and tolerance), then each row evaluated at its own V. Service cases: all rows have the same y₀ (by construction), so the rows are ranked by M_max, which is how Module 02's D/C rule ranks them, so the envelope row equals Module 02.
  - Toggle off, single pile, integral abutment, linear / LPILE lateral basis: unchanged (the code paths are not entered; `solvePyResFor(gPM)` / `runOne(gPM)` with the omitted shear are the old calls).
- **Display:** `PmRowTable` (Module 02, Module 11, printed 02 and 11): columns Row, n piles, f_m, [p-mult], V per pile (kip), share (% of V_total), M_max, y₀ = y_cap, flexure D/C, combined D/C, lateral status (with the failing checks named); title "… equal head deflection — governing row k (f_m, V)"; note with V_total, y_cap, Σ n·V, the largest row y₀ difference and the tolerance, iterations and extra solves (or the reason it failed). Envelope rows "· row k (f_m x.xx, V x.xx)" and the notes; Lateral graphs pushover design point at the governing row's V; report 02 "Lateral load applied (governing row k)"; report H-pile "Lateral / moment" with the governing row's V.
- **Governing provision:** AASHTO LRFD Bridge Design Specifications, 10th Ed. (2024), Art. 10.7.2.4 and Table 10.7.2.4-1 (row p-multipliers, unchanged; the commentary's group analysis assumes the cap distributes the lateral load to the piles); the rigid-cap condition (all pile heads deflect equally) as in FHWA GEC-12 (FHWA-NHI-16-009) group lateral analysis and the GROUP / LPILE group procedure — verify the article references. No p-y curve, p-multiplier, resistance factor or check formula changed; what changed is the shear each row is solved and checked with.

+/* ============================================================
+   F33 (O42, 2026-10-11): RIGID-CAP EQUAL-DEFLECTION LATERAL DISTRIBUTION BY ROW
+   ------------------------------------------------------------
+   Used only with "Apply group p-multipliers automatically (per row)" on in Pile group
+   mode (groupPmAutoOn). Before F33 every row was solved with the same per-pile shear
+   (the rigid-cap equal share V). A rigid cap forces every pile head to the same lateral
+   deflection, so the stiffer (leading) rows take more of the cap shear.
+   Unknowns: the per-pile head shear V_k of each row k and the common head deflection
+   y_cap, with
+       y0_k(V_k) = y_cap   for every row k        (y0_k = head deflection of one pile of
+                                                     row k from the nonlinear p-y solve,
+                                                     p-multiplier = row f_m x modifier)
+       sum_k n_k V_k = V_total = V x sum_k n_k     (n_k = piles in row k; V = the case's
+                                                     per-pile lateral load)
+   The head moment, the axial load and the head condition (fixed / free / rotational
+   spring) are the case's, the same for every row (the tool's existing per-pile rule).
+   Method (the solver is load-controlled, so the iteration is on the row shears):
+   multi-row secant iteration. Each row is linearised as y0_k ~ y_k + s_k (V - V_k),
+   s_k = the secant slope dy0/dV through the row's two latest solves (the first step
+   uses the secant through the origin, y_k / V_k, or a probe solve when V_k = 0). The
+   linear system gives y* = [V_total - sum n_k V_k + sum n_k y_k / s_k] / sum (n_k / s_k)
+   and V_k <- V_k + (y* - y_k) / s_k, which meets sum n_k V_k = V_total exactly; every
+   row is then re-solved. A trial load at which a row's solve does not converge is
+   halved back toward the last good load (twice); a row that cannot be solved at the
+   halved load, or needs halving in 3 iterations in a row, is declared "did not converge"
+   at the load it needs.
+   Converged when sum n_k V_k = V_total (to 1e-9 relative) and every row's y0 is within
+   EQD_TOL_REL x |y_cap| (or EQD_TOL_ABS) of y_cap = sum n_k y0_k / sum n_k.
+   solve(k, V) returns a p-y result with .ok and .headDefl_in (in); init[k] is the row's
+   solve at V (reused, so the first iterate is the pre-F33 equal-share result).
+============================================================ */
+const EQD_TOL_REL = 5e-4;   // 0.05 % of y_cap
+const EQD_TOL_ABS = 1e-5;   // in
+const EQD_MAX_IT = 25;
+function eqDeflDistribute({ nPer, Vpile, init, solve }) {
+  const nR = nPer.length;
+  const N = nPer.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0);
+  const Vtot = (Vpile || 0) * N;
+  const okOf = r => !!(r && r.ok && isFinite(r.headDefl_in));
+  let nSolves = 0;
+  const S = (k, V) => { nSolves++; return solve(k, V); };
+  const cur = new Array(nR).fill(null), prev = new Array(nR).fill(null), nBack = new Array(nR).fill(0);
+  const out = (ok, extra) => {
+    const y = cur.map(c => c ? c.y : null);
+    const yCap = cur.every(c => c) ? cur.reduce((a, c, k) => a + nPer[k] * c.y, 0) / N : null;
+    const sumNV = cur.every(c => c) ? cur.reduce((a, c, k) => a + nPer[k] * c.V, 0) : null;
+    const spread = yCap != null ? Math.max(...cur.map(c => Math.abs(c.y - yCap))) : null;
+    return Object.assign({ ok, V: cur.map(c => c ? c.V : null), res: cur.map(c => c ? c.res : null), y, yCap, Vtot, sumNV, spread, N, nPer: nPer.slice(),
+      tolRel: EQD_TOL_REL, tolAbs: EQD_TOL_ABS, nSolves }, extra);
+  };
+  // starting points: the equal-share solves; a row that did not converge there starts lower
+  for (let k = 0; k < nR; k++) {
+    let V = Vpile || 0, r = init[k], h = 0;
+    while (!okOf(r) && h < 4 && Math.abs(V) > 1e-9) { V = V / 2; r = S(k, V); h++; }
+    if (!okOf(r)) return out(false, { failRow: k, failV: Vpile || 0, it: 0, why: "row " + (k + 1) + " did not converge at the equal share or at reduced loads" });
+    cur[k] = { V, y: r.headDefl_in, res: r }; prev[k] = null;
+  }
+  const slope = k => {
+    const c = cur[k], p = prev[k];
+    if (p && Math.abs(c.V - p.V) > 1e-9 * Math.max(1, Math.abs(c.V))) {
+      const s = (c.y - p.y) / (c.V - p.V);
+      if (isFinite(s) && s > 0) return s;
+    }
+    if (c.s > 0) return c.s;                                  // keep the last good slope
+    if (Math.abs(c.V) > 1e-9) { const s = c.y / c.V; if (isFinite(s) && s > 0) return s; }
+    return null;
+  };
+  for (let it = 0; it <= EQD_MAX_IT; it++) {
+    const yCap = cur.reduce((a, c, k) => a + nPer[k] * c.y, 0) / N;
+    const sumNV = cur.reduce((a, c, k) => a + nPer[k] * c.V, 0);
+    const spread = Math.max(...cur.map(c => Math.abs(c.y - yCap)));
+    if (Math.abs(sumNV - Vtot) <= 1e-9 * Math.max(1, Math.abs(Vtot)) && spread <= Math.max(EQD_TOL_REL * Math.abs(yCap), EQD_TOL_ABS)) return out(true, { it });
+    if (it === EQD_MAX_IT) break;
+    // slopes; a row with none (V = 0 and no previous point) gets a probe solve
+    const s = [];
+    for (let k = 0; k < nR; k++) {
+      let sk = slope(k);
+      if (sk == null) {
+        const dV = Math.max(0.25 * Math.abs(Vpile || 0), 0.5);
+        const r = S(k, cur[k].V + dV);
+        if (!okOf(r)) return out(false, { failRow: k, failV: cur[k].V + dV, it, why: "row " + (k + 1) + " did not converge at the probe load" });
+        prev[k] = cur[k]; cur[k] = { V: cur[k].V + dV, y: r.headDefl_in, res: r };
+        sk = slope(k);
+        if (sk == null) return out(false, { failRow: k, failV: cur[k].V, it, why: "row " + (k + 1) + ": head deflection does not increase with the shear (post-critical)" });
+      }
+      cur[k].s = sk; s.push(sk);
+    }
+    let num = Vtot, den = 0;
+    for (let k = 0; k < nR; k++) { num += nPer[k] * (cur[k].y / s[k] - cur[k].V); den += nPer[k] / s[k]; }
+    const yStar = num / den;
